analysis.title: Stablecoins 2025: Everything you should know in 10 slides
key_insights: Stablecoin market cap rose from $20bn in 2020 to $246bn in May 2025, about 7.0% of total crypto market cap, and stablecoins are the quote currency in over two-thirds of crypto transactions.
Tether (USDT) grew from $67bn in June 2022 to over $149bn in May 2025 and is 62% of the total stablecoin market cap.
Stablecoins processed $27.6trn in transactions in 2024, higher than Visa and Mastercard. Transaction count is up 598% since 2020.
Payments and remittances via stablecoins cost under 3%, against about 6% for traditional systems. Visa is partnering with Bridge for LatAm cross-border payments and invested in BVNK.
83% of fiat-pegged stablecoins are USD-backed. Stablecoins hold over $120bn in USD reserves, and Tether holds $99bn in US T-bills, making it a top holder of US debt.
Issuer reserves resemble money-market funds. Tether holds about $98bn (81% of reserves) in Treasuries, Circle about $24bn (up from about $12bn in Dec 2022), and Ripple about $70mn in T-bills.

Active stablecoin wallet addresses rose from 22.8mn in Feb 2024 to over 35mn in Feb 2025, a 53% increase. Stablecoin mentions in SEC filings averaged 103 a month in Feb-April 2025, against 48 a month from Jan 2024 to Jan 2025.

DB still expects the GENIUS Act to pass by August 2025 despite Senate resistance and concerns that Trump's family-backed World Liberty could profit from it. GENIUS requires 100% reserve backing, federal charters and audits.
GENIUS allows algorithmic stablecoins conditionally, while the STABLE Act bans them for two years. DB expects GENIUS to put pressure on offshore issuers such as Tether to comply or risk exclusion.

Other regulation: the EU approved 10 stablecoin issuers under MiCA in March (Tether excluded). The UK FCA proposed issuance rules in April and will exempt overseas issuers. Hong Kong's stablecoin bill has its second reading expected May 21.
Treasury's implied projection has T-bills held by stablecoin issuers rising from $0.12trn in 2024 to $1.00trn in 2028, an 8.3x increase.

Stablecoin adoption would raise demand for US Treasuries and shift demand to the front end of the curve, since GENIUS requires issuers to hold T-bills under 93 days. It could also pressure banks to pay more for deposits or use wholesale funding.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Stablecoins are now a core source of crypto liquidity.

macro_indicators.indicator: US T-bills held by stablecoin issuers (Treasury implied projection)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Implies a large rise in stablecoin issuer demand for short-dated Treasuries.

crypto_views: Stablecoins are nearing mainstream adoption in 2025 as the GENIUS and STABLE Acts move through the US Congress.
USDT is 62% of stablecoin market cap and the main systemic risk. A depeg or run on USDT would hit crypto markets and possibly US Treasuries through mass asset liquidation.
Tether has never completed a full independent audit, and neither the GENIUS nor the STABLE Act properly regulates offshore issuers such as Tether.
PayPal announced in April that customers can soon receive 3.7% yield on its PYUSD stablecoin.

Visa survey: users prefer stablecoins over banks for yield (45%), efficiency (41%) and lower interference risk (39%). 38% of users in Nigeria, Indonesia, Turkey, Brazil and India use stablecoins to hedge inflation.
risk_factors: Lack of audit at offshore issuers such as Tether.
Systemic risk from a depeg or run on USDT.
Illicit finance and sanctions evasion, which the GENIUS Act only partly addresses.
US legislative delay or political resistance to GENIUS.
charts_described: Stablecoin transfer volumes vs Visa and Mastercard: $27.6trn in 2024 for stablecoins, higher than Visa and Mastercard.
Treasury implied growth projection for T-bills held by stablecoin issuers: $0.12trn in 2024 to $1.00trn in 2028, 8.3x.
geopolitical: Russia is considering a yuan-pegged stablecoin to circumvent sanctions.
Stablecoins are valued as a hedge against geopolitical turmoil and April's tariff volatility, when average supply rose 1.8% from March to $218bn.
World Liberty, a Trump family-backed firm, struck a $2bn investment with the UAE over its USD1 stablecoin.

tension_points.bull_case: DB still expects the GENIUS bill by August 2025, which would accelerate institutional and corporate adoption and legitimize regulated issuers such as USDC.
tension_points.bear_case: The bill faces political resistance over concerns that Trump seeks to profit from it, via World Liberty's $2bn UAE deal, and Senate resistance last week.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The bill failing to pass by the August 2025 target.
